lines.text: The robot must also face the right way. Turning uses the same three ideas.
A top spin rate, the fastest spin it can still stop from, and gentle near the end.
It brakes its turn early too, and stops turning within a third of a degree.
It turns the short way, and since it's a swerve robot, it drives and turns at once.
Now a route with a corner. The simple way: stop at the corner, then start the next leg.
Stop, go, stop, go. Precise, but slow.
Drive To Pose can pass through a waypoint instead, handing over just before the corner.
The hand-over happens on a circle at most forty centimeters from the corner.
How fast through the corner? Like a car: a gentle bend quickly, a hairpin slowly.
It picks the fastest speed whose curve fits inside the corner.
